assumptions: binary rules with |l|, |r| <= 5 and ternary rules with |l|, |r| <= 3 for the potential
length-preserving binary rules with bordered lhs, |l| = 4, 5, words <= 10 for confluence/RD
meta.falsification: A rule with no admissible (c, K), a step violating the constant change, or a confluent length-preserving rule without random descent.
meta.hypothesis: H-C04-3: for every rule l -> r (l != r) there are a letter c, an exponent K and delta != 0 such that Phi(w) = sum over positions i with w_i = c of i^K (or Phi = |w| if |l| != |r|) satisfies Phi(v) = Phi(u) + delta for every step u -> v. Hence all derivations between two words have equal length, and a terminating one-rule system is confluent iff it has random descent.
meta.methodology: Construct (c, K, delta) as in the proof (first letter whose position power sums differ, least K); check Phi(v) - Phi(u) = delta on every one-step pair from every word up to length 7. Separately compare confluence and random descent on exhaustive derivation graphs.
meta.question: Why did no terminating one-rule system turn out confluent without random descent?
meta.title: Constant-step potentials for one-rule systems; confluence versus random descent

summary: constant-step potential verified for 5365 rules on 470927 one-step pairs: 0 violations (largest exponent K needed: 2)
